results.title: RSS during Manipur violence: From seva to efforts for peace and reconciliation
results.description: IMPHAL: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), with more than a century of service to society and the nation, has witnessed growing expectations from people during times of crisis. This was also evident during the recent five-day visit (November 16–20) of Param Pujaniya Sarsanghchalak Dr Mohan Bhagwat to Assam and Manipur, particularly Manipur, which continues to be marred by prolonged ethnic violence. Driven by the spirit of serving society, RSS swayamsevaks have been extending voluntary services during national crises since the British era. From running relief camps during the Partition of Bharat and volunteering during the 1962 Bharat-China War and the 1965 Bharat-Pakistan War to establishing a Model Relief Centre at Haraorou during the peak of violence in Manipur in 2023, the Sangh has continued its service activities. The Model Relief Center, which was established on June 17 accommodated 110 displaced persons fully by Swayamsevaks. Since the outbreak of violence in May 3, 2023, RSS karyakartas have also been providing essential commodities and other assistance to internally displaced people in Manipur. Read more: RSS Foundation Day 2026: From partition relief to national security, a century of service and sacrifice From its involvement in the integration of Goa and Dadra and Nagar Haveli to its peace initiatives in Manipur, the organisation, which envisions making Bharat a Vishwaguru, has consistently emphasised national integration and the protection of Manipur’s territorial integrity. Swayamsevaks have been rendering services in different violence-affected areas of the state while also making efforts to bridge the growing social divide. Since the outbreak of violence, RSS karyakartas have been mobilised to undertake various seva karya. These include the distribution of essential items to relief camps, running the Model Relief Centre at Haraorou, providing free residential educational facilities, organising psychological counselling and yoga sessions and free coaching classes, and conducting vocational training programmes for internally displaced people in Manipur and outside the state. The organisation has also extending financial assistance to the next of kin of those who lost their lives during the violence. Besides the seva karya undertaken directly by the Sangh, several humanitarian initiatives have been carried out in collaboration with like-minded organisations and through the voluntary efforts of individual swayamsevaks. On June 18, 2023, the RSS appealed to the government, including the local administration, police, military and central agencies, to take every possible step to immediately stop the violence and restore peace in Manipur. “The Sangh appeals to the government, including the local administration, police, military and the central agencies, to take every possible step to immediately stop this painful spate of violence, ensure a seamless supply of relief materials among the displaced, along with necessary actions to maintain peace and harmony,” RSS Sarkaryawah Dattatreya Hosabale said in a statement, while affirming the Sangh’s solidarity with the internally displaced people. Read more: Manipur violence: RSS appeals for peace, says ‘no place for hatred in a democratic setup’ The statement also appealed to civil society organisations, political groups and the people of Manipur to take every possible step to end the prevailing cycle of violence and work towards lasting peace. It emphasised the need to overcome the trust deficit through comprehensive efforts from both communities, addressing the sense of insecurity and helplessness among the Meiteis as well as the genuine concerns of the Kuki community. RSS Sarsanghchalak Dr. Mohan Bhagwat also expressed concern over the situation in Manipur during his Vijayadashami address delivered from Nagpur on October 24, 2023. In his address, he raised several questions concerning the possible involvement of extremists from across the border, the interests of external forces and the geopolitical significance of Manipur. Read more: “Were extremists from across the border also among those who committed violence in Manipur?” RSS’ Mohan Bhagwat Referring to the long history of coexistence between the Meitei and Kuki communities, the RSS Sarsanghchalak questioned how mutual discord and hatred had suddenly erupted in a state that had experienced relative peace for several years. He also questioned whether extremists from across the border were involved in the violence and who had attempted to give a communal colour to the conflict between the two communities. Raising concerns about possible external interference, RSS Sarsanghchalak questioned whether foreign powers were seeking to take advantage of the unrest and instability in Manipur. He also drew attention to the geopolitics of Southeast Asia, considering Manipur’s strategic location in the region. Drawing the attention to recurring incidents of violence whenever positive steps towards peace appeared to be emerging, the Sarsanghchalak of RSS further questioned who was responsible for sustaining the violence despite the presence of a strong government at the Centre and a state government that wanted to maintain the peace that had prevailed over the preceding nine years. Emphasising the need for a comprehensive approach to resolving the crisis, Mohan Jee said that multidimensional efforts, strong political will, concurrent action and administrative efficiency would be required. He particularly underlined the role of enlightened social leadership in bridging the gap of mutual distrust that had developed between the two communities. He also acknowledged the contribution of swayamsevaks who were continuously engaged in serving people irrespective of community affiliations and organising relief activities. He expressed pride in the swayamsevaks and other volunteers who had made dedicated efforts to help people and provide assistance during the difficult situation in Manipur. Apart from the local karyakartas, senior RSS national functionaries have also made continuous efforts to reach out to people affected by the violence in Manipur. During his visit on September 8, 2023, RSS Sah Sarkaryawah Mukund CR visited Leitanpokpi and Dolaithabi villages in Imphal East district, which had witnessed extensive destruction during the ongoing Meitei-Kuki ethnic conflict. He also visited various relief camps, interacted with the affected people and met members of the respective camp committees. During the visit, he appealed to the people of Manipur and other stakeholders to work towards bringing peace and restoring normalcy in the state.
